## Find the centre and radius of c
Compare with $x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$: here $2g = -4$, $2f = 2$ and $c = -4$.
g &= -2, \quad f = 1
The centre is $(-g, -f)$, so $A = (2, -1)$.
r &= \sqrt{g^2 + f^2 - c}
&= \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4}
&= 3
## Find the distance from A to B
|AB|^2 &= (5-2)^2 + (8-(-1))^2
&= 9 + 81
&= 90
## Use Pythagoras in triangle ATB
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so $\angle ATB = 90^\circ$.
|BT|^2 &= |AB|^2 - |AT|^2
&= 90 - 9
&= 81
|BT| &= 9
ANSWER: |BT| = 9

## Write the centre and use the point (1, 4)
The centre is on the $x$-axis, so let it be $(h, 0)$. The point $(1,4)$ is $5$ units from the centre.
(1-h)^2 + (4-0)^2 &= 5^2
(1-h)^2 + 16 &= 25
(1-h)^2 &= 9
## Solve for h
Take the square root of both sides: $1 - h = 3$ or $1 - h = -3$.
h &= -2 \text{ or } h = 4
## Write both equations
Each circle has radius $5$, so use $(x-h)^2 + y^2 = 25$.
c_1: \quad (x+2)^2 + y^2 &= 25
c_2: \quad (x-4)^2 + y^2 &= 25
ANSWER: c_1: (x+2)^2 + y^2 = 25, \quad c_2: (x-4)^2 + y^2 = 25

## Find the angles in triangle EFH
The angle of elevation $52^\circ$ is $\angle HFG$, so $\angle EFH$ is on a straight line with it.
|\angle EFH| &= 180^\circ - 52^\circ
&= 128^\circ
|\angle FHE| &= 180^\circ - 35^\circ - 128^\circ
&= 17^\circ
## Use the sine rule to find |HF|
\frac{|HF|}{\sin 35^\circ} &= \frac{6}{\sin 17^\circ}
|HF| &= \frac{6\sin 35^\circ}{\sin 17^\circ}
&= 11.771
## Find the angles in triangle HFG
The ground slopes at $5^\circ$ and $GH$ is vertical, so $\angle HGF = 90^\circ + 5^\circ$.
|\angle HGF| &= 95^\circ
|\angle GHF| &= 180^\circ - 95^\circ - 52^\circ
&= 33^\circ
## Use the sine rule to find |FG|
Let $x = |FG|$.
\frac{x}{\sin 33^\circ} &= \frac{11.771}{\sin 95^\circ}
x &= \frac{11.771 \sin 33^\circ}{\sin 95^\circ}
&= 6.44
ANSWER: |FG| = 6.44 \text{ m}

## Find the angle between OD and OA
$OA$ and $OB$ are tangents from $O$, so $OD$ bisects $\angle BOA$. $C$ lies on line $OD$.
|\angle DOA| &= \frac{60^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ
## Find |OD| in terms of r
The radius to the point of contact on $OA$ is perpendicular to $OA$, giving a right-angled triangle with hypotenuse $|OD|$.
\sin 30^\circ &= \frac{r}{|OD|}
\frac{1}{2} &= \frac{r}{|OD|}
|OD| &= 2r
## Find the radius of s
$|OC|$ is $|OD|$ plus the radius $|DC| = r$.
|OC| &= 2r + r
&= 3r
## Compare the areas
\text{Area of } c &= \pi r^2
\text{Area of } s &= \pi (3r)^2 = 9\pi r^2
k &= \frac{9\pi r^2}{\pi r^2}
&= 9
ANSWER: k = 9

## Find the area of the triangle COA
Shaded area = sector $OAB$ minus triangle $COA$, so triangle $COA$ = sector $-$ 21.
\text{Sector} &= \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta
&= \frac{1}{2}(7)^2(1.2)
&= 29.4
\text{Area of } \triangle COA &= 29.4 - 21
&= 8.4
## Use the area formula to find |CO|
Triangle $COA$ has sides $|CO|$ and $|OA| = 7$ with angle $1.2$ between them.
\frac{1}{2}|CO|(7)\sin 1.2 &= 8.4
3.5\,|CO|\sin 1.2 &= 8.4
|CO| &= \frac{8.4}{3.5\sin 1.2}
&= 2.5750\ldots
## Subtract from the radius
$B$ and $O$ are 7 cm apart, and $C$ lies between them.
|BC| &= 7 - |CO|
&= 4.4250\ldots
&\approx 4.4
ANSWER: |BC| = 4.4\text{ cm}

## List the sums for two spins
The spinner shows 1, 1, 2, 3, each with probability 1/4, so there are 16 equally likely outcomes.
First spin 1 (twice as likely): second spin 1, 1, 2, 3 gives sums 2, 2, 3, 4.
First spin 2: second spin 1, 1, 2, 3 gives sums 3, 3, 4, 5.
First spin 3: second spin 1, 1, 2, 3 gives sums 4, 4, 5, 6.
## Find the remainder on division by 3
First spin 1 (appears in 2 rows): remainders 2, 2, 0, 1.
First spin 2: remainders 0, 0, 1, 2.
First spin 3: remainders 1, 1, 2, 0.
## Count each remainder and compare
Remainder 0 (Liam): 5 outcomes out of 16.
Remainder 1 (Sorcha): 5 outcomes out of 16.
Remainder 2 (Lee): 6 outcomes out of 16.
The chances are not all equal, so the game is not fair.
ANSWER: \text{No: } P(\text{Lee}) = \tfrac{6}{16} \ne \tfrac{5}{16}

## Probability of VW for each fuel type
P(D \cap VW) &= 0.3 \times 0.7
&= 0.21
P(P \cap VW) &= 0.6 \times 0.25
&= 0.15
P(H \cap VW) &= 0.1 \times 0.09
&= 0.009
## Add the three cases
P(VW) &= 0.21 + 0.15 + 0.009
&= 0.369
ANSWER: P(VW) = 0.369

## Use Pythagoras in the right-angled triangle
The slant height 9 cm is the hypotenuse; the radius 3.3 cm and the height $h$ are the other two sides.
9^2 &= 3.3^2 + h^2
81 &= 10.89 + h^2
h^2 &= 81 - 10.89
h^2 &= 70.11
## Take the square root
h &= \sqrt{70.11}
h &= 8.37
ANSWER: h = 8.37\text{ cm}

## Use the curved surface area formula
\text{CSA} &= \pi r l
&= \pi (3.3)(9)
&= 29.7\pi
&= 93.31
ANSWER: 93.31\text{ cm}^2

## Circumference of the cup rim
When the net is rolled up, the arc of the sector becomes the rim of the cup.
C &= 2\pi r
&= 2\pi (3.3)
&= 6.6\pi
## Arc length of the sector (radius 9)
\text{arc} &= \frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi (9)
&= \frac{18\pi\theta}{360}
&= \frac{\pi\theta}{20}
## Make the arc equal to the rim and solve for the angle
\frac{\pi\theta}{20} &= 6.6\pi
\frac{\theta}{20} &= 6.6
\theta &= 6.6 \times 20
\theta &= 132
ANSWER: \theta = 132^\circ

## Find the radius at F using similar triangles
The small cone down to F is similar to the whole cup: its height is $8.37 - 1 = 7.37$ cm.
\frac{r}{7.37} &= \frac{3.3}{8.37}
r &= \frac{3.3 \times 7.37}{8.37}
r &= 2.9057
## Volume of the cone of water
V &= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h
&= \frac{1}{3}\pi (2.9057)^2 (7.37)
&= 65.16
&= 65.2
ANSWER: 65.2\text{ cm}^3

## Volume of water entering per second
Each second the water forms a cylinder of radius 0.8 cm and length 2.5 cm.
\text{volume per second} &= \pi r^2 \times 2.5
&= \pi (0.8)^2 (2.5)
&= 1.6\pi
&= 5.0265
## Time to fill 65.2 cm³
\text{time} &= \frac{65.2}{5.0265}
&= 12.97
&= 13
ANSWER: 13\text{ seconds}

## Link the radius r and the height h of the water
Let $h$ be the height of the water cone. By similar triangles it has radius $r$ with the same ratio as the whole cup.
\frac{r}{h} &= \frac{3.3}{8.37}
r &= \frac{3.3h}{8.37}
## Put the volume equal to 60
V &= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h
\frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{3.3h}{8.37}\right)^2 h &= 60
\frac{\pi (3.3)^2 h^3}{3(8.37)^2} &= 60
## Solve for h
h^3 &= \frac{60 \times 8.37^2 \times 3}{\pi \times 3.3^2}
h^3 &= 368.59
h &= \sqrt[3]{368.59}
h &= 7.169
## Find the distance below the rim
x &= 8.37 - 7.169
x &= 1.2
ANSWER: x = 1.2\text{ cm}

## Find the z-score for the top 25%
The top 25% starts where 75% of scores lie below, so $P(Z < z) = 0.75$. The tables give $z = 0.68$.
## Substitute into the z-score formula
z &= \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}
\frac{x - 280}{90} &= 0.68
x - 280 &= 0.68 \times 90
x - 280 &= 61.2
x &= 341.2
## Round up to a whole mark
Marks are whole numbers, and 341 is below the cut-off, so the minimum mark is 342.
x &= 342
ANSWER: 342

## Say what the z-scores mean
In the standard normal distribution, $P(-1.96 \le Z \le 1.96) = 0.95$.
So 95% of the data lies within 1.96 standard deviations of the mean. These are the cut-offs used for a 95% confidence interval and a 5% two-tailed test.
ANSWER: 95\%\text{ of values lie between } z=-1.96 \text{ and } z=1.96

## Convert the total weight to an average weight
The total is over 3000 kg exactly when the average of the 40 passengers is over $3000 \div 40$.
\bar{x} &= \frac{3000}{40}
&= 75
## Find the z-score of the sample mean
For means of samples of 40: $\mu = 73$ and standard error $\sigma/\sqrt{n} = 12/\sqrt{40}$.
z &= \frac{75 - 73}{12 / \sqrt{40}}
&= \frac{2}{1.8974}
&= 1.054
## Find the probability
From the tables, $P(Z < 1.054) = 0.8531$.
P(Z > 1.054) &= 1 - P(Z < 1.054)
&= 1 - 0.8531
&= 0.1469
&= 14.69\%
ANSWER: 14.69\%

## Use the median
With 8 numbers the median is the mean of $D$ and $E$.
\frac{D + E}{2} &= 12.5
D + E &= 25
## Use the lower quartile
The lower quartile is the median of $A, B, C, D$, which is the mean of $B$ and $C$.
\frac{B + C}{2} &= 7.5
B + C &= 15
## Use the interquartile range
The upper quartile is the mean of $F$ and $G$.
Q_3 - 7.5 &= 12
Q_3 &= 19.5
\frac{F + G}{2} &= 19.5
F + G &= 39
F + 23 &= 39
F &= 16
## Use the mean
A + B + C + D + E + F + G + H &= 8 \times 13.5
A + B + C + D + E + F + G + H &= 108
A + H + 15 + 25 + 16 + 23 &= 108
A + H + 79 &= 108
A + H &= 29
## Use the range
H - A &= 21
2H &= 29 + 21
H &= 25
A &= 29 - 25
A &= 4
## Split D + E and B + C
$D + E = 25$ with $D < E$ and a gap of at least 2: $D = 12, E = 13$ fails (gap 1) and $D = 10, E = 15$ fails because $F = 16$ is only 1 above 15. So $D = 11$, $E = 14$.
$B + C = 15$ with $C \le 9$ (a gap of at least 2 below $D = 11$) and $B \ge 6$ (a gap of at least 2 above $A = 4$): $B = 6$, $C = 9$. (B = 7, C = 8 is not allowed because $C$ must be at least 2 more than $B$, so $C \ge B + 2$. With $B + C = 15$ this gives $B \le 6.5$, and with $B \ge 6$ this forces $B = 6$.)
## Complete the boxes
The completed boxes are shown in the figure.
ANSWER: A=4,\ B=6,\ C=9,\ D=11,\ E=14,\ F=16,\ G=23,\ H=25

## Find both gaps after t hours
Ship A has moved $15t$ km east, so the east-west gap is $90 - 15t$. Ship B has moved $30t$ km south, so the north-south gap is $30t$.
## Use Pythagoras
s^2 &= (90 - 15t)^2 + (30t)^2
s^2 &= 8100 - 2700t + 225t^2 + 900t^2
s^2 &= 1125t^2 - 2700t + 8100
## Take the square root
Distance is positive, so take the positive root. Ship A reaches the line of Ship B at $t = 90 \div 15 = 6$, which gives the domain $0 \le t \le 6$.
s &= (1125t^2 - 2700t + 8100)^{\frac{1}{2}}
ANSWER: s(t) = (1125t^2 - 2700t + 8100)^{\frac{1}{2}}

## Find the pay for the 45 basic hours
\text{Basic pay} &= 45 \times 12.60
&= 567
## Find the commission on sales above €200
Only the sales above $\text{€}200$ earn commission.
\text{Sales above } \text{€}200 &= 350 - 200
&= 150
\text{Commission} &= 22\% \text{ of } 150
&= 0.22 \times 150
&= 33
## Add basic pay and commission
\text{Gross pay} &= 567 + 33
&= 600
ANSWER: \text{€}600

## Find the pay for the 48 weekday hours
51 hours include 3 on Sunday, so 48 hours are at the basic rate.
48 \times 12.60 &= 604.80
## Find the pay for the 3 Sunday hours
\text{Sunday rate} &= 12.60 \times 1.5
&= 18.90
\text{Sunday pay} &= 3 \times 18.90
&= 56.70
## Add to get the pay before commission
604.80 + 56.70 &= 661.50
## Find the commission paid
\text{Commission} &= 713.20 - 661.50
&= 51.70
## Find the sales above €200
Commission is $22\%$ of the sales above $\text{€}200$, so divide by $0.22$.
\text{Sales above } \text{€}200 &= 51.70 \div 0.22
&= 235
## Add back the first €200 of sales
\text{Total sales} &= 235 + 200
&= 435
ANSWER: \text{€}435

## Tax the income up to the cut-off at 20%
678 \times 0.20 &= 135.60
## Tax the income above the cut-off at 40%
\text{Income above cut-off} &= 713.20 - 678
&= 35.20
\text{Tax at } 40\% &= 35.20 \times 0.40
&= 14.08
## Add to get the gross tax
\text{Gross tax} &= 135.60 + 14.08
&= 149.68
## Subtract the tax credit to get the net tax
\text{Net tax} &= 149.68 - 26
&= 123.68
## Subtract the net tax from the salary
\text{Net income} &= 713.20 - 123.68
&= 589.52
ANSWER: \text{€}589.52

## Multiply every term by the common denominator 12
The denominators 2, 3 and 4 all divide into 12.
\frac{9x-6}{2} &= \frac{3x-14}{3} + \frac{9x}{4}
12\left(\frac{9x-6}{2}\right) &= 12\left(\frac{3x-14}{3}\right) + 12\left(\frac{9x}{4}\right)
## Cancel each denominator
6(9x-6) &= 4(3x-14) + 3(9x)
## Expand the brackets
54x - 36 &= 12x - 56 + 27x
## Collect like terms
54x - 36 &= 39x - 56
54x - 39x &= -56 + 36
15x &= -20
## Divide both sides by 15
x &= -\frac{20}{15}
x &= -\frac{4}{3}
ANSWER: x = -\frac{4}{3}

## Make y the subject of the linear equation
3x - y &= 4
y &= 3x - 4
## Substitute y = 3x − 4 into the quadratic equation
4x^2 - 3xy &= 4
4x^2 - 3x(3x-4) &= 4
## Expand and collect into a quadratic equal to zero
4x^2 - 9x^2 + 12x &= 4
-5x^2 + 12x &= 4
-5x^2 + 12x - 4 &= 0
Multiply both sides by $-1$ to make the $x^2$ term positive.
5x^2 - 12x + 4 &= 0
## Factorise and solve for x
(5x-2)(x-2) &= 0
5x - 2 &= 0 \quad \text{or} \quad x - 2 = 0
x &= \frac{2}{5} \quad \text{or} \quad x = 2
## Find y when x = 2/5
y &= 3x - 4
y &= 3\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) - 4
y &= \frac{6}{5} - \frac{20}{5}
y &= -\frac{14}{5}
## Find y when x = 2
y &= 3(2) - 4
y &= 6 - 4
y &= 2
ANSWER: \left(\frac{2}{5}, -\frac{14}{5}\right) \text{ and } (2, 2)
